== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-04-the-pilot|The Free [[Worlds]] consist of a cluster of planets that have maintained their independence by remaining outside the reach of the [[Galactic Union]]. While they are smaller in scale than the [[Union]] and larger than the [[Karoshan Alliance]], they are characterized by a high degree of individualism. Unlike the uniform, metal-ringed colonies of the [[Union]], Free [[Worlds]] settlements can take unique forms, such as mining colonies built into mountains. The region lacks a central inter-system government; instead, individual planetary governments manage their own affairs and maintain their own militaries. Historically, the Free [[Worlds]] nearly collapsed when local planetary forces proved insufficient to handle regional problems. This led to the rise of [[the Advocates]], a group that began as vigilantes but eventually gained quasi-official [[Authority|authority]] to provide security and public services for those lacking conventional police protection. In the wake of [[the Advocates]]' fall, many independent companies in the region have sought stability by joining larger corporations.}}

== The Engineer ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-02-the-engineer|Situated on the fringes of civilized space as one of the four corners of the galaxy, the Free [[Worlds]] is a political entity consisting of planets such as [[Murrok]] and the territory of [[Carturus]]. This region lacks a higher inter-system government, though [[the Advocates]] exert significant control over it through represented battlegroups and receive video reports from the area. While the territory contains uncharted planets, its core sectors are swarmed by red dots on sector maps, leading to the targeting of nearby planets. Despite a deep hatred for the [[Vallenar Corporation]] and their potential as a group for populations in the [[Thevellian System]] to join, the crew eventually finds themselves needing to leave the region after traveling toward it.}}
